# A Store leaks the Model it creates and destroys a Model it borrows

## Context

Found while reviewing PR #20449 (the practical Store guide for #7224). Its teardown section tells readers to destroy `store.model` after `store.destroy()`, because the author saw a provider-created Store's Model stay registered after the provider ended. A guide should not have to teach that. I re-measured it on dev `03f88c6992` with a Node probe on the engine's unit setup (`test/playwright/setup.mjs`).

## The Problem

A Store that receives a Model **class or config** creates the Model instance itself. `Store#destroy()` never retires that instance. The Model stays registered in `Neo.manager.Instance`, and its `RecordFactory` record class stays cached under `Neo.data.record.<className>.<modelId>`. Every Store lifetime leaks both: a grid closed with its tab, a provider-owned Store when its view ends, a field-created ComboBox Store when its form closes.

Ownership is also inverted on replacement. `beforeSetModel()` destroys the old Model even when it was a **borrowed instance** that another Store or field still routes through.

```
(a)  after destroy: store destroyed = true | model registered = true | model.isDestroyed = false | record class ns = true
     control: borrowed model still registered after its borrower is destroyed = true
(a2) borrowed model after `store.model = StateModel`: isDestroyed = true
```

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/Store.mjs`: `beforeSetModel()` runs `oldValue?.destroy()` and then `ClassSystemUtil.beforeSetInstance(value, Model)`. That call creates an instance from a class or config and returns an instance unchanged. `destroy()` detaches the `allItems` forwarding, unregisters, and calls `collection.Base#destroy()`, which retires `allItems`, filters and sorters but not `model`.
- `src/core/Base.mjs` `destroy()` deletes own properties. It destroys no instance-valued config.
- `src/data/RecordFactory.mjs` caches one record class per Model instance (`${recordNamespace}.${model.className}.${model.id}`). That class closes over the Model, and every record reads its schema through it (`getField()`, `fieldsMap`, `hasNestedFields`), on reads (`record.get()`) as well as on field sets.
- Records outlive their Store. `test/playwright/unit/form/field/Chip.spec.mjs`, "replaces its owned Store only after the shared chip projection detaches", re-resolves a record of the Chip field's destroyed Store by its key. ComboBox's `afterSetStore()` does the same for "a record of a store destroyed below".
- Sibling precedent: `ComboBox#destroyOwnedStore()` destroys the Store it created and then only the Model it created. That private view Model creates no records, so destroying it is safe.

Design authority: the engine's own ownership JSDoc on the same Store/Model pair, `ComboBox#owned`: "Stores created by this field and the Models created for its private views. A passed or bound Store and its Model remain outside this set." The stateful-owner rule states the same thing in general: "one owner ends its lifetime (the creator destroys what it created; a borrowed handle is released, never destroyed)" (neo-agent-skills `pr-review/audits/core-idiom-audit.md`, check 5).

## The Fix

- `Store` records whether `beforeSetModel()` created the instance, i.e. the value was not already a `NeoInstance`.
- A Model the Store created is **released, not destroyed**, when the Store ends or replaces it. Records keep reading it, so the Store drops only the global references that keep it reachable: its `Neo.manager.Instance` entry and its cached record class. The Model is then collected with the last record that still reads it.
- The Store never releases or destroys a passed Model instance.
- `Model#destroy()` also drops its cached record class, so an explicitly destroyed Model, such as ComboBox's private view Model, leaves none behind.

Why release and not destroy, measured: a destroy-based first cut made a retained record's next field set throw (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'has')`) and failed the Chip spec above, because `record.get()` reads the destroyed Model.

## Contract Ledger

Two roots keep a Model reachable: the `Neo.manager.Instance` registry, keyed by id, and the `Neo.data.record.<className>.<id>` record-class cache. A record keeps its Model reachable through its class closure.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Boundary / fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Store#beforeSetModel()` | `ComboBox#owned` JSDoc; the stateful-owner rule | Decides once whether the Store created the Model (anything but a `NeoInstance`). On replacement it releases a Model it created. | A passed instance is never released or destroyed. The Store's existing records keep working through the released Model. | `@summary` | `Store.spec.mjs` › "replacing a Model the Store created releases it; its records keep working"; "a passed Model instance stays its owner's, on destroy and on replacement" |
| `Store#destroy()` | Same | After its own teardown, releases a Model it created. | A retained record still reads and writes (it notifies nobody, since the Store is gone). A passed instance stays its owner's. | `@summary` | › "destroy() releases a Model the Store created from a class" / "… from a config" |
| `Model#release()` (new) | `Chip.spec.mjs` re-resolving a retained record | Drops this Model's registry entry and its cached record class, each only while it still names this Model. Does not destroy. | A repeated or late call after a successor reused the id removes nothing of the successor's. The Model is collected with its last record. | `@summary` | › "a released Model whose id a successor reused retires nothing of the successor's" (late-release arm) |
| `Model#destroy()` (override) | Same as above; explicit destroy is the owner's statement that the schema is done | Drops its own cached record class, then the core destroy. | A record retained past an explicitly destroyed Model fails on its next field set. That is unchanged and is why the Store releases instead. A destroy after a successor reused the id leaves the successor registered with its class. | `@summary` | Same test (first-destroy arm); "a passed Model…" last arm |
| `RecordFactory#releaseRecordClass()` (new) | The cache it owns | Deletes the cache entry only while it holds the class built for this Model (tracked per Model). | Records created earlier keep their class. | `@summary` | Id-reuse arm |
| `manager.Base#unregister()` | `core.Base#afterSetId()`: ids "need to stay unique at any given point" | A key removes its entry. A reference removes itself only while it still holds its key's registration. | All current callers pass a key or the registered object, so their behavior is unchanged (caller census in PR #20457). | `@summary` | Id-reuse arm (instance manager); Engine unit census at head |
| `core.Base#destroy()`, bootstrap `Neo.idMap` fallback | Same | Before `Neo.manager.Instance` exists, a destroy deletes its `Neo.idMap` entry only while that entry is this instance. | Unchanged once the instance manager is available. | JSDoc line on `destroy()` | Id-reuse arm (bootstrap id map) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On `destroy()`, a Store created with a Model class or config releases that Model: `Neo.get(modelId)` is null and its record class entry is gone. A retained record still reads and writes.
- [ ] Replacing a Store-created Model releases it, and the Store's existing records keep working.
- [ ] A Store given a Model instance never releases or destroys it, on `destroy()` or on replacement.
- [ ] Destroying a Model drops its cached record class.
- [ ] ComboBox still destroys its private view Model, and Chip's re-resolution of a retained record stays green.
- [ ] Red-first: the release and borrowed arms fail on dev.
- [ ] If #20449 has merged: `learn/guides/datahandling/UsingStores.md` no longer tells readers to destroy `store.model`.

## Out of Scope

- `sourceId` views receiving source record edits (the ComboBox picker case is #20453).
- Automatic Model cloning, which #20403 excluded.
- Redesigning the `RecordFactory` class cache.

## Avoided Traps

- Do not destroy a Store-created Model. Records outlive the Store and read their schema through it (measured above).
- Do not touch a passed instance. It has another owner.
- Do not key ownership on `className` or on a shared-Model registry. The created-vs-passed decision is made once, in `beforeSetModel()`.
